Objection 1 (AC-4 and AC-5 carried verify:"test" with no CI case behind them) — ACCEPTED, both removed from acceptance[]. qa.md requires a verify:"test" criterion to cite "ci" in test_ids, forbids fabricating that citation, and makes verdict:pass impossible while any AC is not_covered. I make the scope call explicitly: asserted by qa_script step 9(a), enforced by nothing, and risks[] now says so.

validated_work_order.root_cause: `schedule` and `schedule_occurrence` were introduced as a pair by #7, but #7 only ever taught the WRITE that creates a stamped row. Every pre-existing write that copies an existing transaction's schedule onto ANOTHER row was left untouched, so the two fields can drift apart and a row can end up schedule-linked with no occurrence identity. `db.updateTransaction` drops undefined fields and keeps explicit nulls (conform() at packages/loot-core/src/server/aql/schema-helpers.ts:136, which returns null for an undefined field and the result is .filter(Boolean)-ed away), which is why these paths silently leave the stamp at its existing value instead of erroring.
validated_work_order.approach:
One rule, applied at every place that copies a transaction's schedule onto another row: the occurrence stamp travels with the schedule link, or not at all.

I re-audited every write that propagates `schedule` from one transaction to another. There are exactly four, all in this change: merge.ts:165 (split branch of mergeTransactionsNoTransfer), merge.ts:176 (normal branch), transfer.ts:68 (addTransfer, constructing the mirror leg), transfer.ts:131 (updateTransfer, rewriting the mirror leg).

Two other sites carry `schedule` and are deliberately NOT touched. transfer.ts:83 and :89 write `matchedSchedule` back onto the SAME transaction whose stamp is already correct — nothing is copied between rows. forecast-schedules.ts:273 copies `schedule` onto a simulated transfer leg that is never persisted (its sourceTransaction is built at :218 with no stamp to copy). find-schedules.ts:29's `schedule: null` is a query filter, not a write.

On the merge expression I specify `??` rather than the `||` used on the line above. A stamp is either a positive YYYYMMDD integer or null, so the two operators agree on every reachable value; `??` states "take the dropped row's only when the kept row has none" without implying 0 is a meaningful date. It is a deliberate difference from the surrounding line and the reviewer should read it as one.

On updateTransfer I specify `transaction.schedule_occurrence` verbatim rather than `?? null`, and this is load-bearing. Because conform() drops undefined but writes null, a partial update that omits the field leaves the mirror alone — exactly how the schedule line above it already behaves — while an explicit null from the client clears the stamp alongside the schedule link. I verified all three behaviours with a probe rather than reasoning about them: with the fix applied, a full update leaves the mirror stamped, a partial update omitting the field leaves it stamped, and an explicit null clears it. `?? null` would have wiped the mirror's stamp on every partial API update that never mentioned it.

The migration fix is a one-byte append. Migrations are keyed by filename, not content, so an already-migrated database is unaffected.

No release note: the behaviour this corrects shipped unreleased with #7, whose note (upcoming-release-notes/keep-posted-schedules-paid-today.md) is still pending, so there is nothing for a second note to tell a user about.

qa_script: Bring the app up (`yarn start`, or `yarn start:server-dev`), open a budget with 'View demo' so there is real data to merge against.

Schedules page: create a recurring schedule — a name, a fixed amount (e.g. 100 out), a monthly date condition on a specific day. Post its current occurrence with the schedule's post/Pay action. Confirm the schedule now reads as paid for that occurrence.
In that account's register, manually add a second transaction with the SAME amount dated roughly three weeks EARLIER than the posted one. It must be the identical amount — merge refuses a mismatch.
Select exactly those two rows and use Merge. Confirm one row survives and still carries the schedule link.
Reload and return to the Schedules page. The occurrence must still read as paid. Before this fix it flips back to 'Due' and the upcoming row comes back — that flip is the bug AC-1 names.

Transfer leg (expected to be a no-op on screen, confirm it stays one): take a schedule-posted transaction and change its payee to another account's transfer payee. A mirror row appears in the other account. Nothing may duplicate, disappear, or change the schedule's paid status.
Repeat step 6 by editing the main leg's date afterwards. The mirror must still track it and the schedule must still read as paid.

No new console errors, and no new rows in either account's register beyond the expected mirror. (If step 6 produced TWO mirror rows instead of one, the update re-routed through addTransfer — that is the trap named in the transfer.test.ts cases, and it is a real defect in this change, not a test artefact.)

Mechanical checks — run all three and require each to pass before reporting QA green. (a) MIGRATION NEWLINE: `tail -c 1 packages/loot-core/migrations/1790969762045_add_schedule_occurrence_to_transactions.sql | xxd` must print `00000000: 0a`; it prints `00000000: 3b` on unmodified main, so this is a real check, not a tautology. (b) NO SNAPSHOT CHURN: `git diff --stat "$(git merge-base HEAD main)" -- packages/loot-core/src/server/transactions/__snapshots__/` must print nothing at all. (c) SUITE GREEN, NO `-u`: run `yarn workspace @actual-app/core run test:node` with NO `-u` flag; require exit code 0, and require that `git status --porcelain -- packages/loot-core/src/server/transactions/__snapshots__/` printed nothing afterwards. Do NOT check the pass/test/file counts — this PR adds nine new cases to three existing test files, so any count pinned in the plan is unreachable by a correct implementation. AC-2 and AC-3 are the execution path for (c); (a) and (b) are the execution path for the migration-newline fix and the no-churn constraint, which no CI case can prove.
risks: The merge change means a kept row can acquire a stamp it did not have, sourced from the dropped row. The invariant that makes this safe is that stamp and schedule link are written by the SAME expression, so they can never disagree: `schedule: keep.schedule || drop.schedule` picks keep's schedule whenever keep has one, and in that case keep necessarily has a meaningful stamp or none at all. If a future edit ever decouples those two lines the invariant breaks, so keep them adjacent.

The transfer change means two rows can now match the same occurrence. Every consumer of getHasTransactionsQuery collapses to a Set of schedule ids or a boolean — schedules/app.ts:602, schedules/app.ts:654 and desktop-client/src/hooks/useSchedules.ts:34 — so an additional matching row cannot change any of their outcomes. I re-read all three this round; none counts rows.

The migration's trailing newline is enforced by NOTHING, and no CI check can enforce it. The pre-commit hook runs oxfmt over `**/*.{js,mjs,jsx,ts,tsx,md,json,yml,yaml}` — `.sql` is not in that glob, so the hook never sees a migration file. v2 claimed this property was "already enforced by .nano-staged on every commit in this repo", which was false, and the plan review was right to reject it. I also tested the suggested remedy: adding `**/*.sql` to the oxfmt glob would NOT work, because oxfmt 0.59.0 refuses .sql outright — pointed at a directory containing only a .sql file it prints "Expected at least one target file" and leaves the file byte-identical, and pointed at the file explicitly with --check it exits 0 having formatted nothing. So the glob entry would be a no-op that reads like enforcement. The property is asserted by qa_script step 9(a) and nothing more; recorded here so the next planner does not inherit a false premise a third time.

The no-snapshot-churn constraint is likewise not CI-provable: a .snap file IS the expected value, so a PR that edits it can still be green. It is enforced by requiring the new transfer cases to assert on db.all rows (tests[]) and by qa_script step 9(b).

forecast-schedules.ts:273 propagates `schedule` to a simulated transfer leg without a stamp and is deliberately left alone. It is not a write path — the row is never persisted — but a future change that persists forecast rows would have to revisit it.

QA step 9(b) uses `git merge-base HEAD main` rather than a literal ref, because the branch under test may not be called main and QA may be on a detached HEAD. If main does not resolve, the command fails loudly rather than silently diffing against the wrong base — the safe direction.

No new hosts, no network calls, no new dependencies. Nothing in this change touches a forbidden_paths entry: packages/loot-core/migrations/** is not among them (only packages/ci-actions/src/migrations/**, packages/loot-core/src/mocks/migrations/** and packages/loot-core/src/server/migrate/** are), so the migration edit is permitted.

alternatives_considered.approach: Cover the migration-newline and no-snapshot-churn constraints with test cases instead of qa_script steps (a node test that reads the migration's last byte; a test that shells out to `git diff` on the snapshot directory).
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The shell-out half is a worse execution path than a QA command: it couples the unit suite to git state and the working directory, and fails on a shallow clone or detached HEAD where the diff base cannot resolve. The migration-byte half is not merely inelegant but impossible to make CI-enforced here, which I verified this round — oxfmt 0.59.0 refuses .sql outright, so the formatting hook can never enforce it and only a bespoke test could. Neither constraint survives as an acceptance criterion that CI can honestly prove, so both were removed from acceptance[] rather than left self-contradicting, exactly as the plan review required.

alternatives_considered.approach: Add `**/*.sql` to the oxfmt glob in .nano-staged.json so the pre-commit hook enforces the trailing newline on every future migration — the alternative the plan review explicitly offered.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It does not work, and I tested it rather than assuming. oxfmt 0.59.0 does not format .sql: pointed at a directory containing only a .sql file it errors with "Expected at least one target file", leaves the byte unchanged, and under --check exits 0 having checked nothing. The entry would be a no-op that reads like enforcement — the same false premise the review just rejected, one layer down. It is also a change to every contributor's commit hook, which is a maintainer's call, not this ticket's.

assumptions: `schedule_occurrence` can only ever be null or a positive YYYYMMDD integer (the migration declares it INTEGER and #7 writes schedule.next_date through it), so `??` and `||` behave identically here and no falsy-but-valid stamp exists.

The desktop client sends a whole transaction entity on edit, so transaction.schedule_occurrence is present when the UI updates a schedule-posted transaction. This is why updateTransfer can pass the value through verbatim; a caller that sends only `{ id, notes }` leaves the mirror's stamp alone — the intended-and-safe direction, which I verified with the probe rather than assuming.

db.getTransaction returns rows read back through the AQL schema, so keep.schedule_occurrence / drop.schedule_occurrence are null rather than undefined for an unstamped row — either way `??` treats them the same.

Merges of two transactions that are each stamped for DIFFERENT schedules already pick one schedule (`keep.schedule || drop.schedule`); this change makes the stamp follow that same pick rather than introducing a new selection rule.

`date` on a db.insertTransaction call is a plain 'YYYY-MM-DD' string and `schedule_occurrence` likewise, not an integer. Both throw `Invalid date` from convertInputType if passed as an integer or as a toDateRepr value; I hit this twice while probing and the affected tests[] entries name it.

validated_work_order.debate_summary: No council ran on this replan. The decision in front of me was the v2 plan review's three objections, and I accepted all three — each was correct on its facts and each is now discharged rather than argued around. Objection 1 (AC-4 and AC-5 carried verify:"test" with no CI case and no real execution path): both are removed from acceptance[], the migration byte check survives as qa_script step 9(a) with the one-byte fix still in files[], and the no-churn constraint moved into the tests[] entries that carry it plus risks[]. Objection 2 (step 9(c) pinned `1212 passed / 2 skipped / 87 files`, a number measured before the nine new cases existed, so a correct implementation would fail it): every pinned count is gone from qa_script, acceptance, evidence[] and residual_risks[], replaced by exit code 0, no -u, and no snapshot file written. Objection 3 (the claim that .nano-staged already enforced the trailing newline was false): corrected, and I went past the objection's own remedy — it suggested adding `**/*.sql` to the oxfmt glob, and I tested that and found oxfmt 0.59.0 refuses .sql outright, so the entry would be inert. I make the scope call explicitly: assert it in QA, enforce it by nothing, and say so in risks[] so the next planner does not inherit the false premise a third time. Beyond the three objections I found two further errors and corrected them on the merits: the review's premise that every other migration ends with a newline is false (5 of 55 pre-existing files do not, so ours is a 49-of-55 majority-convention fix), and my own first two probes were wrong in ways that would have produced tests that pass while proving nothing (an integer where the column wants a 'YYYY-MM-DD' string; a transfer payload missing transfer_id, which re-routes to addTransfer and creates a duplicate mirror instead of updating the existing one) — both are now named in the tests[] entries. The diagnosis and the three-file diff are unchanged from v2, but nothing is inherited on trust: findings 1 and 3 were re-reproduced with fresh probes, the fix was re-probed, the suite and typecheck were re-run, and the tree was reverted clean.
residual_risks: In addTransfer, runRules may assign a different schedule to the mirror leg than the main leg's (`matchedSchedule = schedule ?? transaction.schedule`). The stamp is copied unconditionally alongside it, so in that (unverified) case the mirror would carry a schedule and a stamp belonging to different schedules. Pre-existing behaviour of the `schedule` field on the same object; a guard, if one is ever wanted, belongs on both fields together.

The migration's trailing newline and the no-snapshot-churn constraint are enforced at QA time by commands, not by CI. A future change could reintroduce either without any test failing. This is a deliberate trade — no test can prove a file's last byte or that a .snap file was untouched, and the one automated route for the former is demonstrably unavailable — but it does mean those two guarantees are only as good as whoever runs qa_script step 9.

The nine new test cases raise the node suite's pass count above what any earlier note recorded. Nothing in the pipeline pins a count, but a human comparing a CI run against an older plan should expect the number to have moved and should read exit code rather than a total.
